title: Intel CFO at Deutsche Bank Technology Conference, 2026-Aug-26
gist: Notes from Intel's CFO at the August 2026 Deutsche Bank Technology Conference show 18A yields beating internal milestones, 14A defect density ahead of its target curve with the 0.9 PDK due in October, growing external customer engagement on 14A, and EMIB-T advanced packaging projected to become a multi-billion-dollar-per-customer annual business by 2029 — even as Intel Foundry still runs roughly a $2.5 billion quarterly loss.

insights.claim: Intel's 18A process yields are progressing and beating the milestones the company set internally, according to Intel's CFO.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Yields beating internal targets on 18A is a positive execution signal for Intel's foundry turnaround narrative, relevant to gauging whether Intel can hit its external customer commitments on schedule.
insights.quote: 18A yields are progressing, beating the milestones that we've internally set

insights.claim: Intel's 14A process defect density is tracking better than the company's internal target curve, and Intel expects to deliver the 0.9 version of the 14A process design kit (PDK) in October 2026.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Ahead-of-curve defect density plus a concrete October 2026 PDK delivery date gives investors a near-term, checkable milestone for tracking Intel 14A's actual execution versus guidance.
insights.quote: 14A, when you look at the defect density is tracking better than the target curve we had
insights.locator: 14A, when you look at the defect density

insights.claim: Intel is now seeing internal-customer demand for its 14A process, and CEO Lip-Bu Tan and his team are meeting with external customers on 14A on a weekly basis.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Weekly CEO-level engagement with external 14A customers signals Intel treats external foundry customer wins on 14A as an urgent near-term priority, a signal to watch for actual signed customer announcements.
insights.locator: Lip-Bu and the team are now meeting on a weekly basis

insights.claim: Intel's CFO said the company feels very confident in its advanced packaging position, particularly EMIB-T, which is expected to generate multiple billion dollars of revenue per customer per year, ramping in the second half of 2027, becoming a run-rate business in 2028, and hitting its stride in 2029.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A multi-billion-dollar-per-customer-per-year revenue projection for EMIB-T gives investors a concrete, dated ramp (2027 ramp, 2028 run-rate, 2029 full stride) to model Intel Foundry's packaging revenue trajectory against.
insights.quote: it (EMIB-T) will be multiple billion dollars per customer per year of business.. ramp in the back half of 2027, a run rate business in 2028, hitting its stride in 2029
insights.locator: we're performing in terms of advanced packaging

insights.claim: Under CEO Lip-Bu Tan, Intel has cut organizational layers from 12 down to 6 and reduced the number of vice presidents from roughly 450 to about 200.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A halving of management layers and a more than 50% cut in VP headcount is a substantial cost and decision-speed lever, relevant to modeling Intel's operating-expense trajectory under Lip-Bu Tan.
insights.quote: he (Lip-Bu Tan) collapsed the number of layers of the organization.. from 12 down to 6.. eliminated VPs from 450 to maybe 200
insights.locator: he (Lip-Bu Tan) collapsed the number of layers

insights.claim: Intel Foundry is currently running at approximately a $2.5 billion loss per quarter, according to the CFO's remarks.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A roughly $2.5B quarterly foundry loss sets the financial baseline against which any 18A/14A yield improvements and EMIB-T packaging revenue ramp must be weighed to judge when Intel Foundry could approach breakeven.
insights.quote: (Intel Foundry) running at like a $2.5 billion loss or so per quarter
insights.locator: (Intel Foundry) running at like a $2.5 billion loss
